outcome.answer: Yes. A training-free LLM active-learning framework proposes materials experiments directly from text descriptions in an iterative few-shot setting, without training a task-specific model; it reports reaching top-performing candidates with over 70% fewer experiments than the compared approaches [1]. LLMs can also suggest novel battery-material candidates through analogy-guided reasoning [2]. These approaches select or generate suggestions, but the abstracts do not establish that LLM proposals are automatically reliable; experimental validation remains important.
